newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt to lay off up to 40,000 staff - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt to lay off up to 40,000 staff - report.

text.p: The Brazilian government plans to lay off up to 40,000 federal government workers out of a total of 540,000 under its voluntary program which is being launched in November, a newsPaper said.

Brazil's minister for public administration Luiz Carlos Bresser Pereira said it was too early to say exactly how many staff would take part in the program, but it would be somewhere between 20,000 and 40,000 workers, according to O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper.
"I don't think we can talk exact numbers yet," he was quoted as saying by O Estado. "I don't think, for example, that we will reach 40,000."
Bresser Pereira said the aim of the program was to create incentives for staff to leave their jobs in areas where excess personnel existed.

He said the government was in the final stages of defining the terms of the voluntary redundancy program which would provide compensation for federal public workers based on the number of years of employment.
A further 70,000 public sector jobs which are vacant at present will be eliminated and another 20,000 positions will disappear once the current holders retire, Bresser Pereira added.
The government is also still studying the closure of state- owned companies, O Estado said.
Bresser Pereira said an inter-ministerial working group was studying a preliminary list of 23 state-owned firms to determine exactly how many and which companies would be shut down.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
